question.text: Find all the values of $x$ that satisfy $2x-5 > 1$ or $2x - 7 < 13.$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $2x-5 > 1\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2x-5 &> 1 \\ 2x &> 6\\ x &> 3 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $2x - 7 < 13\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2x - 7 &< 13\\ 2x &< 20 \\ x &< 10 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $x < 10$ or $x >3.$ We can write this using interval notation as $x \in(-\infty, \infty).$

question.text: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $5x-1 > 7$ or $2 \leq 2x+5 < 16.$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $5x-1 > 7\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 5x-1 &> 7\\ 5x &> 8 \\ x &> \dfrac{8}{5} \end{align*}

Then, we solve $2 \leq 2x+5 < 16\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2 &\leq 2x+5 < 16 \\ 2-5 &\leq 2x < 16-5 \\ -3 &\leq 2x < 11\\ -\dfrac{3}{2} &\leq x < \dfrac{11}{2} \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $x \geq -\dfrac 3 2.$ We can write this using interval notation as $\left[-\dfrac{3}{2},\infty \right).$

question.text: Find all the values of $x$ that satisfy $3x+5 > 11$ or $2x - 3 \le 1.$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $3x+5 > 11\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3x+5 &> 11 \\ 3x &> 6\\ x &> 2 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $2x - 3 \le 1\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2x - 3 &\le 1\\ 2x & \le 4 \\ x & \le 2 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $x \le 2$ or $x > 2.$ We can write this using interval notation as

\[ x \in (-\infty,\infty). \]

question.text: What is the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $6 \leq 3x+9 \leq 15$ or $4x-3 \geq 5?$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $6 \leq 3x+9 \leq 15\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 6 &\leq 3x+9 \leq 15 \\ -3 &\leq 3x \leq 6 \\ -1 &\leq x \leq 2 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $4x-3 \geq 5\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 4x-3 & \geq 5 \\ 4x &\geq 8 \\ x &\geq 2 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $x\geq -1.$

question.text: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $-8 \lt 4x-4 \lt 8$ or $2-x > 3.$
question.explanation:
We start by solving $-8 \lt 4x-4 \lt 8\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} -8 &\lt 4x-4 \lt 8 \\ -4 &\lt 4x \lt 12 \\ -1 &\lt x \lt 3 \end{align*}

Then, we solve $2-x > 3\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 2-x &> 3 \\ -x &> 1 \\ \dfrac{-x}{-1} &< \dfrac{1}{-1} \\ x &< -1 \end{align*}

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

Therefore, the final solution is $-1 \lt x \lt 3$ or $x < -1.$ We can write this using interval notation as $(-\infty,-1) \cup (-1,3).$
